title: Every rank occurs as a sorting position
statement: Let $kf:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ and let $N,q\in\mathbb N$ with $q<N$. Define the sorting position of $j$ as the number of indices $m<N$ with $kf(m)<kf(j)$, plus the number of indices $m<j$ with $kf(m)=kf(j)$. Then some $j<N$ has sorting position $q$.
